newsitem.title: ITALY: Three held on suspicion of laundering Mafia money.
newsitem.headline: Three held on suspicion of laundering Mafia money.

text.p: Three businessmen were arrested on Saturday on suspicion of laundering millions of dollars of "dirty money" for jailed Mafia boss Pippo Calo, Italian police said.
Police in the Sicilian capital of Palermo identified the three men as Luigi Faldetta, 58, Vincenzo Bellino, 54, and Giuseppe Bellino, 35.

The three, who face charges of Mafia assocation, are suspected of running the business affairs of Calo, who has served 12 years of a life sentence for ordering a train bombing which killed 16 people in 1984.

Police said they believed that several companies alleged to be owned by Calo and managed by the three men had laundered millions of dollars of illegally earned money through investments in real estate in Sicily and Sardinia.
The companies have been put under judicial sequester.
Calo was one of the most feared members of the Corleone Mafia clan and managed its interests in Rome.
He was described by Giovanni Falcone, a leading anti-Mafia magistrate murdered in 1992, as "a man who commissioned murders and who was also a link between Mafia criminals and white-collar criminals".
Calo made headlines again last month when it emerged that he was being probed for ordering the murder in 1982 of Italian banker Roberto Calvi.
Calvi, known as "God's banker" because of his alleged links with Vatican circles, was found hanging from a bridge in London in June 1982 with his pockets stuffed with bricks.
Calvi was chairman of the defunct bank Banco Ambrosiano, whose collapse with huge debts after his death was one of the biggest frauds in Italian business history.
